subject: Renewal: mid-term seat increase, co-term and credit options
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel@greenline.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenline.ai
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-term increase and co-term options for RW-2197

Hi Rachel,

Hope you had a good weekend. We’re seeing faster-than-expected adoption of Redwood for a new internal product and need to increase our committed seat capacity mid-contract. Current renewal is Feb 2027 (co-term would be helpful), and procurement asked if there’s a way to: 1) apply any unused committed capacity credits from our current term, 2) get a short-term uplift price for the increased seat band while we assess usage, and 3) co-term the new capacity to Feb 2027 rather than add a standalone annual.

Can you outline options and what approvals you’d need to move quickly? I attached a short note with our projected seat curve.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform
Greenline Analytics

Attachment: greenline_seat_projection_may2026.pdf
From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@greenline.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term increase and co-term options for RW-2197

Hi Daniel — thanks for the note and the projection. Happy to help. High level options we typically offer for mid-term increases:

- Option A: Pro-rata add-on (no co-term) — new seats billed monthly pro-rata, standard pay-as-you-go uplift pricing. No credits applied.
- Option B: Mid-term committed uplift (co-term to Feb 2027) — we add committed seats for the remainder of your term. We can apply unused portion of your original commitment as a credit against the uplift on a pro-rata basis.
- Option C: Temporary burst + evaluation — short (30–60 day) burst at discounted uplift rate while you validate usage, then convert to committed with co-term.

I’ve looped in Rishi for concrete numbers and Neha for procurement steps (SOW/PO and DocuSign). Can you confirm the target seat increase (approx %) and whether procurement needs an invoice-first flow?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Daniel Park <daniel@greenline.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term increase and co-term options for RW-2197

Thanks Rachel. Daniel — based on the projections attached and historical usage, here’s a practical proposal to get you immediate capacity with reasonable economics:

1) Short-term uplift (60 days) for +30% seats at a 12% uplift to your current committed unit price. This gets capacity live while we confirm steady-state.

2) If Greenline converts the uplift to committed capacity and co-terms to Feb 28, 2027 within those 60 days, we’ll:
   - Apply remaining unused committed credits from your current agreement as a one-time credit against the converted committed seats (pro-rated).
   - Reduce the committed uplift price to 6% above current pricing (effective start date of converted commitment).

3) Procurement flows: Neha — to enable co-term conversion we can prepare a short amendment + DocuSign. If they require invoice-first, we can do an interim invoice for the uplift period.

I attached two files: a line-item uplift proposal and a pricing model with pro-rate examples.

Next steps: Daniel — confirm target delta (we used +30% in the attached model), whether Greenline will consider a 60-day validation window, and any internal approval timelines.

Thanks,
Rishi
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Greenline_RW-2197_uplift_proposal_v1.pdf; Greenline_PRICING_MODELS.xlsx
From: Daniel Park <daniel@greenline.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@greenline.ai
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term increase and co-term options for RW-2197

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Rishi. A few clarifying questions before we run this up the chain:

- Can you confirm how the unused credit calculation works? We pre-paid for 12 months in Jan; if we convert in June with 7 months left, how much credit will apply and how is rounding handled?
- If we do the 60-day uplift and don't convert, will we be charged the full 12% uplift for those 60 days only (i.e., no retroactive conversion charges)?
- For the co-term conversion doc: procurement prefers an amendment rather than a whole new MSA. Can you send a redline we can share with legal?

Procurement also asked for a tie to usage thresholds — e.g., conversion only if average daily active seat consumption > 80% of the uplifted quantity during the validation window. Is that acceptable?

Thanks — getting eyes on this Wednesday, will revert with procurement feedback.

Best,
Daniel

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.inference.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@greenline.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.inference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-term increase and co-term options for RW-2197

Thanks Daniel — all reasonable asks. Quick confirms and next steps: 

- Unused credit: we compute a pro-rata credit based on remaining days in the original committed term multiplied by the committed seat rate. Example: if you have 7 months remaining, credit = (7/12) * monthly committed spend allocated to seats. We’ll provide the precise dollar calc in the amendment.
- 60-day uplift: charged only for the uplifted period at the uplift rate (12%). No retroactive uplift if you convert; instead you’ll receive the conversion credit applied at conversion per Rishi’s note and then the converted committed rate (6% uplift) applies going forward.
- Validation threshold: 80% average daily consumption is fine as the conversion trigger; we’ll include measurement method (rolling 60-day average of daily seat count as reported in Console).

Attached: co-term_redline.docx (first pass amendment redline). I’ll also open a HubSpot task for Neha to generate the amendment + interim invoice if needed. Daniel — when you’re ready I can send the DocuSign envelope; we can also route invoice-first if procurement insists.

DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/console/envelope/0a1b2c3d4e
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345678/timeline
